origin.description: Extract every complete match from each string. A string with no match contributes an empty character vector.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: Input vector. Either a character vector, or something coercible to one.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Pattern to look for. A plain character vector is a regular expression. fixed compares literal text, coll uses collation, and boundary matches character, word, line, or sentence boundaries. The empty string is a character boundary.

arguments.name: simplify
arguments.text: FALSE, the default, returns a list of character vectors. TRUE binds those vectors into a character matrix and pads short rows with empty strings.

origin.details: Recycling and names follow the other stringr search functions. simplify must be a single TRUE or FALSE. The empty pattern and boundary() extract every boundary segment. A miss is omitted. simplify = TRUE of an all-missing result is a matrix with no columns.
origin.value: A list of character vectors the same length as string or pattern, or a character matrix when simplify is TRUE.
origin.example:
shopping_list <- c("apples x4", "bag of flour", "bag of sugar", "milk x2")
str_extract_all(shopping_list, "[a-z]+")

translation.description: Extract every complete match from each string. A string with no match contributes an empty list.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A string, stringi._na.NA, or a list of those. A list may carry names.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: A plain string or list is an ICU regular expression. fixed, coll, regex, and boundary return Pattern objects and select that engine. The empty string is a character boundary.

arguments.name: simplify
arguments.text: False, the default, returns a list of character vectors. True binds those vectors into a character matrix and pads short rows with empty strings. Any other value is an error.

translation.details: check_lengths raises RecycleError when lengths other than 0 and 1 disagree. simplify is checked with the same TRUE-or-FALSE rule as rlang's check_bool. Empty and bound call stri_extract_all_boundaries. The other engines call the matching stri_extract_all function. Every call passes omit_no_match=True. Names on string are kept when pattern has length 1 or the same length as string.
translation.value: A list of character vectors, or a list of rows when simplify is true. A missing string is a one-element NA vector. A miss is an empty vector. NA is stringi._na.NA.
translation.example:
from stringr.extract import str_extract_all
shopping_list = ["apples x4", "bag of flour", "bag of sugar", "milk x2"]
print(str_extract_all(shopping_list, "[a-z]+"))
